audience_text:
One row is: one inpatient census event for a patient, representing that patient being counted in a bedded location on a particular census date.

Who's in it: patients with a census event during the chosen reporting period, linked to a patient record, in the chosen service area or areas and chosen location or locations. Choosing All for service area includes every service area. Choosing All for location includes every location. The report is limited to departments other than CCMC EMERGENCY, CCMC IR IMAGING, CCMC CATH LAB, CCMC MAIN OR, CCMC SPA OR, CCMC PHP PSYCHIATRY, CCMC CARDIOVASCULAR OR, and DSC OR.

Each row shows: the patient’s census placement, the clinical setting involved, the patient’s hospital class and service, the event timing, and identifying details for the related ADT and location records.

Time window: it includes census events whose effective time falls from the chosen start date through the chosen end date, including the whole end date. It shows the data as it stood at the end of the chosen as-of date, so only events entered by then are included. Canceled census events are still shown if they were not deleted until after the as-of date, which means they still existed in the record at that point in time.

Excludes: records not linked to a patient; the listed excluded departments; events outside the chosen date range; events entered after the as-of date; and census events that had already been canceled and deleted by the end of the as-of date.

This selection contains census ADT events for patients whose event time falls during the chosen date range, using the event date up to and including the end date, and showing the data as it existed on the chosen As Of date. It includes events that were still active then, and also events later marked canceled if they were not deleted until after that As Of date, so the report reflects what staff would have seen at that point in time.

For each included event, it shows the patient, census day, patient class, patient service, department, room, bed, service area, and the event’s create and delete timestamps, along with the event’s identifiers. Excludes records without a patient, records that do not match the separately defined required linked selections, and events in these departments: CCMC EMERGENCY, CCMC IR IMAGING, CCMC CATH LAB, CCMC MAIN OR, CCMC SPA OR, CCMC PHP PSYCHIATRY, CCMC CARDIOVASCULAR OR, and DSC OR.

This selection is the list of service areas chosen when running the report. It includes either the specific service area where a department sits, or the choice All, which brings in every service area.

It is built from hospital location setup and bed and room setup, with ADT history and patient class information available to support how those departments and locations are used in the inpatient setting. Each selected service area is carried forward once as a reporting choice for the rest of the dataset.

This selection is one chosen location value when running the report: either **All** or one specific **revenue location linked to the department**. It is used to keep ADT bed history aligned to the hospital location structure, so activity can be limited to the chosen revenue location or include every location when **All** is chosen.

In practical terms, it ties bed, room, department, service area, and patient class information to each ADT event for a hospital encounter. It also carries a simple marker showing the chosen location entry is active in this dataset build.

This field shows the type of patient movement event recorded for the row; in this data it will read Census, meaning a census-related bed or patient location event rather than another kind of ADT activity. For business users, that tells you the row is about inpatient census tracking.

This field tells you the subtype recorded for the census event, which is the specific kind of census movement or status change for that patient event. In business terms, it is the label that further describes what kind of census event happened, beyond simply knowing it was a census event.

This field is the date and time when the census event actually took effect for the patient, such as when a bed status or location change became active in the hospital census. For business users, this is the operational timestamp to use when you want to know when that census status truly started, which can differ from when someone entered the event into the record.

This field is the patient’s identifier from the medical record, so it tells you which patient each census event belongs to. In business terms, it is the value you would use to distinguish one patient from another and to link this row to that patient’s other activity in the record.

This field shows the abbreviated patient class for the encounter tied to the census event, such as the short label used in the record for whether the patient is inpatient, outpatient, observation, or another class. For business readers, it is the concise category that tells you what kind of hospital stay or visit this bed or census event belongs to.

This field shows the abbreviated name of the department tied to the patient’s census event, so it tells you which clinical department or unit the patient was assigned to in shorthand form. In practice, this is the short department label staff would recognize for where the patient was placed, rather than the full department name.
This field shows the name of the room tied to the patient’s census bed event, so it is the room staff would recognize on the unit where the patient was placed or assigned at that point in care.

This field shows the label of the bed tied to the patient’s census event, in other words the bed name staff would recognize on the unit. It tells the business reader which specific bed the patient was assigned to at that point in their stay.

This field shows the patient service name for the census event, meaning the clinical service the patient was assigned to at that point in their stay, such as the team or specialty responsible for their inpatient care. For business readers, it tells you which service line was managing the patient when that census snapshot was recorded.

This field shows the date and time when that census event record was deleted from the system. In practice, it lets you see whether an event was later removed after it had been entered, which is useful when reviewing changes or understanding why an event no longer counts as an active census entry.

This is the date and time when the census event was entered in the record. For business use, it tells you when that bed or patient movement update was documented, which can be different from when the event actually took effect.

This field shows the name of the service area attached to the event, so it tells you which service line or operational area the patient activity belongs to in the organization. For business users, it is the plain-language service area name rather than the internal identifier.

This field is the identifier of the department tied to the census event, so it tells you which clinical department or unit the patient’s bed status was recorded under. In practice, this is the department value used to place the patient in the right care area for reporting, excluding the specific procedural and emergency departments that are intentionally left out of this dataset.

This field is the identifier of the room tied to the patient’s census bed placement event, so it tells you which room the patient was assigned to at that point in their stay. In business terms, it is the room-level location value used to place the patient within the hospital.

This field shows the identifier of the bed tied to that census event, meaning the specific bed the patient was occupying for that recorded inpatient bed-status moment. For business users, it is the bed-level value used to place the patient in an exact bed rather than just a room, unit, or department.

This is the unique identifier for the individual census event record, so it distinguishes one bed or unit census event from another in the data. For business users, it is mainly a technical tracking number you can use to tie this row back to the exact underlying event if you need to validate or investigate it.

This field gives the calendar day taken from the event’s effective time, so it tells you which census date the bed or patient status belongs to. In practice, it is the day the census event counts on for reporting, not the exact timestamp.
